ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary federal AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. Relevant sanctions legislation includes the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21. Federal corporate beneficial ownership requirements for CBCA corporations arise under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, Part XV, including sections 21.1 to 21.303. An Alberta limited partnership is governed principally by the Partnership Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. P-3, and the Limited Partnership Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. L-7. Alberta does not operate a generally equivalent public beneficial ownership register for limited partnerships. Reporting entities must maintain beneficial ownership information under the PCMLTFA regime where applicable.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen every partner, director-equivalent, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, protector, settlor, trustee, senior manager, and material controller before onboarding and at least annually thereafter. Use current United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian sanctions administered under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Screen against applicable United States Office of Foreign Assets Control lists when the business, bank, payment processor, goods, counterparties, or transaction flow has a United States nexus. Apply a documented PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate assessment under the PCMLTFA framework. Obtain senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, enhanced monitoring, and transaction-purpose documentation for foreign and domestic PEP relationships. Resolve name matches using date of birth, nationality, address, identification number, and documentary evidence; do not rely on name-only matches. Report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC where the applicable reporting threshold and statutory test are met, and apply applicable large cash, electronic funds transfer, casino, terrorist-property, and prescribed transaction reporting obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_identification_methodology: Identify every natural person who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25 percent or more of a relevant entity, alone or through affiliates, nominees, trusts, agreements, or concerted-action arrangements. Also identify persons exercising effective control through voting rights, contractual rights, appointment rights, financing arrangements, veto rights, or control of the general partner. For an Alberta limited partnership, document the general partner, all limited partners, ownership percentages, capital and profit interests, voting and consent rights, management rights, transfer restrictions, and any nominee or trust relationship. If no individual meets the ownership threshold, identify the individual exercising control through other means and, only if no controlling individual can reasonably be identified, record the senior managing official in accordance with the applicable reporting-entity rules.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.nominee_and_trust_risk: Nominee arrangements are not a substitute for UBO disclosure. Obtain written nominee declarations, underlying beneficial ownership evidence, trust deeds or extracts where relevant, settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiary, and control information, and legal explanations for any layered ownership. Escalate unexplained nominee ownership, circular ownership, bearer-equivalent arrangements, unexplained third-party funding, or inconsistent ownership information for enhanced due diligence and possible suspicious transaction analysis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry services through an authorized Alberta registry agent; Alberta.ca Corporate Registry is the official government information portal. Alberta limited partnership registrations and business-name filings are generally submitted through authorized registry agents rather than a single unrestricted public self-service incorporation portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the principal language for Alberta registry filings. French documents may require certified translation for practical processing by counterparties or financial institutions. A limited partnership name must comply with the Partnership Act, the Limited Partnership Act, applicable registry requirements, and common-law confusion and passing-off principles. The proposed name must not be misleading, identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, or suggest unauthorized governmental, professional, charitable, or regulated status. Non-Latin characters and transliterations should be pre-cleared with the registry agent; a translated or transliterated name does not eliminate English-language legal-name requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government, Crown, Royal, King, Queen, Alberta, Canada, municipal, federal, provincial, and similar governmental references where they imply official affiliation
Bank, banking, trust, insurance, securities, exchange, credit union, mortgage, finance, investment dealer, portfolio manager, or other regulated-financial terms unless legally authorized
University, college, hospital, police, military, foundation, charity, association, institute, and similar regulated or status-sensitive terms where they create a misleading impression
Lawyer, legal, attorney, accountant, engineer, architect, doctor, pharmacy, and other professional-designation terms where the applicable professional authorization is absent
Words implying licensing, endorsement, royal patronage, public authority, or a business purpose inconsistent with the proposed activities
Offensive, deceptive, fraudulent, or misleading expressions
Name elements that improperly use another person's trademark, corporate name, trade name, or protected business identifier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_qualification: The 30-day value is a conservative transaction-planning assumption required by this schema and must be confirmed with the selected Alberta registry agent. Alberta does not universally provide a single statutory name-reservation period applicable to every limited partnership filing. A name search, reservation, or pre-clearance may have a shorter or different operational validity period, and a reservation does not guarantee final registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written rejection reason and registry-agent transaction reference. Verify whether the issue is confusion, prohibited wording, missing consent, misleading description, trademark risk, or incomplete documentation. Submit revised name options and supporting consent or authorization through the registry agent. If the decision is treated as an administrative decision by a provincial authority, request written reconsideration and use the applicable Alberta administrative review or judicial-review process within the prescribed limitation period. The applicant may seek judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench where legally available, but court proceedings do not ordinarily replace the practical remedy of filing an amended name. Preserve search reports, correspondence, consent letters, and evidence of distinctiveness. Do not market or contract under a rejected name before valid registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_clearance_due_diligence: Search Alberta Corporate Registry records, Canadian federal corporate records, relevant provincial registries, Canadian trademarks through the Canadian Intellectual Property Office, domain names, social-media identifiers, and major marketplace identifiers. Conduct common-law confusion, passing-off, trademark, sanctions, and adverse-media searches before committing to packaging, inventory, payment accounts, or customer-facing use.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_basis: An Alberta limited partnership must maintain the registered information and Alberta address required by the Partnership Act, the Limited Partnership Act, and applicable registry procedures. The registered address must be capable of receiving legal and official notices. Separate business, records, tax, employment, consumer-protection, and licensing requirements may apply depending on actual operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial virtual office may be acceptable for registry correspondence if it provides a genuine Alberta address, authorized mail receipt, document retention, and reliable access to records. It is generally insufficient as the sole evidence of commercial substance for banking, Stripe, PayPal, tax, customs, consumer-protection, or enhanced AML onboarding. A jewelry and fine-timepiece e-commerce business should maintain verifiable inventory, fulfillment, returns, customer-support, accounting, payment, and management records. If inventory is held outside Alberta, disclose the actual warehouse, fulfillment, and import locations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 5-15 percent annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a normally compliant online retailer with no regulated-license trigger; estimated 15-30 percent during initial enhanced due diligence, complaint investigation, tax review, customs inquiry, payment-processor escalation, unexplained high-value transactions, sanctions concerns, or inconsistent address evidence. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. Federal, provincial, municipal, tax, customs, consumer-protection, landlord, bank, and payment-processor inspections or verification visits are governed by different powers and procedures.
commercial_substance_requirements: Maintain a real Alberta registered office and dependable notice-receipt process.
Maintain the executed limited partnership agreement, amendments, registers, resolutions, accounting records, tax records, and beneficial ownership records.
Document the general partner's management authority and the business reason for using a limited partnership.
Maintain evidence of inventory ownership, supplier contracts, product authenticity, valuation, insurance, shipping, returns, and anti-counterfeiting controls.

Implement customer due diligence proportionate to transaction value and risk, particularly for high-value watches, jewelry, repeated card-not-present transactions, rapid refunds, third-party payments, and unusual delivery destinations.
Obtain municipal business licensing and zoning confirmation if premises, warehousing, showroom, or local fulfillment operations are conducted in Alberta.
Review GST/HST registration, import GST, customs, provincial sales-tax exposure in other provinces, consumer-protection, privacy, electronic-commerce, and product-safety obligations before launch.
industry_specific_risk_controls: Perform enhanced supplier and beneficial-owner screening for luxury goods suppliers and intermediaries.
Verify serial numbers, provenance, invoices, authenticity certificates, export documents, and title to high-value goods.
Prohibit anonymous third-party funding and unexplained overpayments.
Apply transaction, refund, chargeback, and shipping-address monitoring.
Screen customers, suppliers, freight forwarders, and beneficial owners against Canadian, UN, and applicable OFAC sanctions.
Retain records for the periods required by the PCMLTFA, tax laws, payment-provider terms, and applicable consumer and accounting requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), especially section 51; applicable Limited Partnership Regulations; Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 only if environmental triggers apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registries, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta; filings are submitted through licensed Alberta Registry Agents operating on the Corporate Registry System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (prescribed Form 1 under the Limited Partnership Regulations; filed under section 51 of the Partnership Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta limited partnership. No escrow or deposit account is required. Each limited partner's liability is limited to the amount of capital actually contributed or agreed to be contributed under the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The corporate general partner approves the formation of [●] Alberta Limited Partnership under the Partnership Act (Alberta) and subscribes to the general partner interest, agreeing to the initial capital contribution and the admission of all named limited partners. (2) The registered office and principal place of business in Alberta as stated in the Declaration of Limited Partnership is adopted. (3) The officers of the corporate general partner are appointed and authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, to pay all filing fees, to appoint a service agent, and to open bank accounts. (4) The chairperson and any one officer are authorized to execute ancillary documents and to implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registries, Service Alberta (through a licensed Registry Agent using the NUANS name search and electronic reservation window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS pre-search and verify the desired limited partnership name is not confusingly similar to existing Alberta corporations, LLPs, LPs or registered trademarks. Submit the name reservation request electronically through the registry agent. If the name is not reserved, select an alternative or proceed as a numbered limited partnership designated by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Name reservation request form
Identification of the general partner executing the reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the proposed name as confusingly similar, file a revised name reservation or elect a numbered limited partnership designation within any applicable priority period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Partnership Documents and Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate general partner board / private legal counsel; execution before a Commissioner for Oaths or Notary if required by the registry agent or a bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement, then prepare the statutory Declaration of Limited Partnership on Form 1, setting out the LP's name, Alberta jurisdiction, names and addresses of all general and limited partners, capital contributions in cash or property, registered office for service, and term. All general partners must execute the Declaration. The corporate general partner must evidence board authorization of its signatories and the initial capital contribution.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership signed by all general partners
Board resolution or written consent of the corporate general partner
Identification documents for general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is questioned, cure by obtaining fresh signatures, the required commissioning or notarization, and re-issuance of the completed Declaration before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registries, Service Alberta (electronic filing by a licensed Registry Agent on the Corporate Registry System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration, name reservation certificate if applicable, and the government filing fee through the registry agent. The agent transmits the record to the Registrar, who registers the limited partnership and issues the certificate or acknowledgement of registration with the LP number. Confirm the registration date, registered name, and Alberta jurisdiction before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
Name reservation certificate or numbered LP election
Proof of fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of defect or correction, file an amended Declaration or a corrected consolidated Declaration in the prescribed manner and pay any re-filing fee. The limited partnership acquires legal status only when registration becomes effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Bank Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and the financial institution opening the LP operating account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Registration and partnership agreement to obtain a CRA business number for the limited partnership, register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntary registration is desired, and determine whether payroll program accounts are required if employees are engaged. Present the LP registration record to the bank, including the corporate general partner resolution, authorized signatories, and beneficial ownership schedules for KYC.
required_dossiers: Certificate of LP registration
Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
Limited partnership agreement and corporate general partner board resolution
Authorized signatory identification and beneficial ownership schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or the bank flags inconsistencies, reconcile registered names, partner identities, and signatory authority; provide solicitor attestation or corrected registry extracts to complete KYC requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Premises Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal business licensing office in the Alberta municipality of operations, e.g., City of Calgary Business and Local Economy or City of Edmonton Business Licensing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the LP operates from a physical office, store, or warehouse. If premises exist, apply for the municipal business license and any required development or occupancy permit. For pure online or drop-shipping operations without a public-facing storefront, apply for a home-based business license or confirm the municipal exemption for low-impact e-commerce businesses. Obtain landlord consent if subleasing.
required_dossiers: Municipal business license application
Proof of limited partnership registration
Lease or evidence of premises/home occupation authorization
Identification of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or tenancy objection is raised, relocate to a permitted commercial zone or apply for a minor variance or development permit. For home-based businesses, comply with municipal conditions on customer traffic, inventory storage, and signage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Alberta Labour and Immigration (OHS); local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a desktop environmental review confirming that online merchandising of fashion jewelry and watches is not a prescribed activity under Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act. If battery-containing watches are stored, establish waste battery segregation and recycling agreements with a licensed Alberta hauler. Ensure office and warehouse layouts satisfy the Alberta Fire Code and OHS Code, including electrical safety, manual handling of packages, and Workers' Compensation Board coverage if workers are engaged.
required_dossiers: Environmental self-assessment checklist
Waste battery disposal or recycling agreements if battery watches are held in inventory
Fire safety and OHS compliance checklist for the workplace
WCB account registration confirmation if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a fire or environmental inspection identifies non-compliance, implement the corrective action order, obtain a fire safety certificate, and revise battery storage or hazardous waste handling arrangements within the compliance deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no Alberta provincial industrial operating permit applies to ISIC 4791 online retail of fashion jewelry and timepieces. The only operator authorization is the local municipal business license if physical premises are used.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating license is required. The relevant municipal instrument is the Municipal Business License, with a home-based business license if applicable. No manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — online retail sales activity is not listed as a prescribed activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 or its Schedule of Activities; no EIA registration or approval is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or stack-emission thresholds apply. Packaging and municipal solid waste must comply with municipal waste collection bylaws. Button or coin battery handling, if any, must comply with Alberta battery recycling regulations; any liquid hazardous product other than consumer packaging is outside permitted scope and would require a waste storage license.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: occupancy must satisfy the Alberta Fire Code and, where required by the landlord or municipal inspector, fire marshal inspection and an approved fire safety plan. Structural: no special structural load inspection is required for ordinary e-commerce shelving, but commercial racking and storage above prescribed loads must be engineered and inspected under OHS law. Occupational: the general partner must comply with the OHS Act and OHS Code for manual handling, electrical equipment, ergonomic workstation safety, and WCB registration if employees are engaged.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a liberalized foreign exchange regime with full convertibility for current account transactions under the Exchange Control Act. Capital account transactions require prior approval for certain investments exceeding thresholds, but direct equity investments and profit remittances are generally permitted without restriction. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal, subject to tax compliance and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required under Canadian law. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds or convert them at market rates. However, all export transactions must be reported to the Bank of Canada via the Electronic Data Interchange Reporting System (EDIR) if exceeding certain thresholds, with no fixed conversion ratio mandated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions such as Stripe and PayPal offer high cross-border viability for an Alberta LP engaged in online jewelry and watches merchandising. Legal constraints include mandatory FINTRAC registration as a money services business, enhanced due diligence for high-risk merchant categories, and adherence to FATF standards. Offshore digital EMIs must navigate potential CFC attribution rules and transfer pricing documentation requirements when facilitating cross-border flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote online account opening is permitted for Canadian Limited Partnerships under Alberta corporate law, subject to video KYC verification and digital document submission. Physical presence is not mandated for standard onboarding; however, directors or authorized signatories may be required to attend in-person interviews or provide additional verification for transactions exceeding CAD 50,000 or in cases of heightened AML risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source of funds or unexplained large inbound remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed trade invoices, customer purchase records, shipping manifests, and proof of goods provenance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure lacking transparency or involving complex offshore entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited partnership agreement, corporate registry filings, beneficial ownership declarations, and tax identification numbers

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign partners or investors are processed via SWIFT international wire transfers to the LP's Canadian dollar account at a Tier 1 bank. Required purpose codes include 'EQTY' for equity contributions or 'LOAN' for intercompany loans. Verification protocols mandate supporting documentation such as subscription agreements, capital contribution notices, and CRA Form T1134 for reporting foreign property holdings. All transfers are subject to FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting and beneficial ownership verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements are facilitated through SWIFT MT103 messages for wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit via correspondent banks. For jewelry and fine timepieces, payments to suppliers are routed in CAD or freely convertible currencies, supported by underlying commercial invoices, purchase orders, and delivery confirmations. All outflows comply with export control regulations and anti-money laundering screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for hedging specific currency exposures
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for managing offshore currency risks
